maria (sec-eng): FYI Acme Security asked for end-to-end audit evidence for a FedRAMP-style review: per-tenant RBAC mappings, KMS-signed audit bundles, and realtime event validation into their SIEM. They want clarity on what we can commit in contract/SLA and rough timeline.

oliver (cs): Quick q — when they say 'KMS-signed audit bundle' do they expect our KMS to sign exports (proof of possession) or a signature made by a service key we rotate? Also asked about retention windows.

maria (sec-eng): They specifically asked for vendor-signed bundles verifiable against our cert chain (auditor needs chain-of-custody), retention 7 years for flagged auth/policy events, and a schema that maps roles->tenant ids for auditor consumption.

alex (eng-sre): Tech notes: required additions to event schema: actor_role, tenant_id, kms_signature, signature_alg, audit_schema_v. We should expose an export endpoint like /audit/export/{tenant} that returns tar.gz + detached .sig (PKCS7 or RSA-PSS). Signing large exports will need an async worker pool and HSM/KMS throughput considerations — perf hit estimated.

alex (eng-sre): ```json
{
  "event_type": "auth.change",
  "actor_id": "user:123",
  "actor_role": "admin",
  "tenant_id": "tenant:acme",
  "resource": "model:prod",
  "action": "grant",
  "result": "success",
  "kms_signature": "<base64>",
  "signature_alg": "RSA-PSS",
  "audit_schema_v": "2026-03-01"
}
```

jamie (legal): Contract/SLA questions: what's our time-to-deliver for a signed bundle on request? Is a vendor-signed PKCS7 adequate for non-repudiation? FedRAMP auditors often want timestamping or TSA assertions on top of signatures. We should loop in compliance counsel.

maria (sec-eng): Suggest we define two delivery tiers: standard — on-demand export within 72h (best-effort signing); SLA'd — 48h with dedicated capacity + attestation (billable). Also need acceptance criteria: schema conformance + signature verification + explicit rules about allowed redactions.

oliver (cs): They want near-real-time push to their SIEM (CEF/Splunk HEC) for critical auth/policy changes. Can we provide signed streaming or at least attestable webhook batches?

alex (eng-sre): Per-message KMS signatures are expensive. Options: signed JWT envelope per-batch, or HMAC per-message using a shared secret. HMAC is lighter but weaker legally vs KMS-signed exports. We should document tradeoffs clearly.

sec-bot: RFC-5467 opened by @alex: audit-export-signing-and-rbac-schema — https://gh/repo/pull/5467

maria (sec-eng): Action items: @alex prototype schema + export flow + perf/ops estimate; @oliver confirm customer acceptance criteria and SIEM format; @jamie draft contract addendum (SLA/fees) and escalate TSA/timestamp question to compliance. I'll assemble acceptance test set (sample events + verification steps).

alex (eng-sre): Ack. Will spike tomorrow and aim for a PR by EOW.

oliver (cs): I'll set up a short call with Acme to walk requirements and share sample SIEM mapping.

jamie (legal): Looping in compliance counsel — note that FedRAMP moderate vs high changes the level of attestation required; I'll clarify which baseline Acme is targeting.

maria (sec-eng): Thanks all. tagging this thread into incidents & audit RFCs and keeping thread as single source for deliverable owners. :white_check_mark:
